name_reason: Canonical, convention-compliant, and semantically grounded. Prefix data_fd2_ + battle domain (battle core dispatch table) + _table reflects the data type (90-entry function-pointer array). The name pairs 1:1 with the sibling scalar data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_idx @ 0x51A8F: enemy-AI/turn loops (fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0/1, fd2_run_full_turn_cycle, player action menus) latch an index into that scalar, then dispatch table[idx](char_idx) as the battle post-action consequence (counter/death/status proc) -- the symbol's primary runtime role. The chapter-event-handler aspect is the CONTENT of the slots (all targets are fd2_chapter_event_handler_NN__*), which the home-file comment already documents. Renaming would be net-negative: it would desync an established name used across src (btltab.c, btl_ai.c, btl_turn.c, menu.c, menufld.c, globals.h) and KB (battle.md, chapter_event_dispatch.md, field_map.md, fdfield.md, _index.md) and break the _idx/_table pairing. No Ghidra address residue: _table is a data-type descriptor, not a hex suffix; no domain ID involved.
purpose: 90-entry dispatch table of chapter-event handler function pointers (void(*)(uint32)); the battle AI/turn-loop post-action consequence dispatch target, also reused directly by FDFIELD tile-event, turn-event, and kill-drop event paths.
logic_summary: Each of the 90 slots holds the entry address of one fd2_chapter_event_handler_NN__* function (NN = 2-digit hex slot index; targets span 0x341DB..0x360FE, the contiguous chapter-event handler block). Indexed by an 8-bit event id; the handler is tail-called as a single-arg cdecl (active char_idx) with ADD ESP,4 cleanup, so element type is void(*)(uint32). Two dispatch idioms: (1) primary battle path -- AI/turn loops set data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_idx @ 0x51A8F (0xFF = none) and, if != 0xFF on the next iteration, call table[idx](char_idx) (counter/death/status proc), resetting the latch to 0xFF; (2) direct path -- fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction (field-map event tile, entry type 'other'), fd2_fire_chapter_turn_events_for_phase (turn-gated chapter scripts, entry .event_id), and fd2_process_battle_drop_entries (kill-drop entry type 2) load the table base with a literal [idx*4 + 0x51B91] (these are the only three xrefs Ghidra reports). Several 'unref_*' slots have no reachable in-game event id but are emitted verbatim to preserve the 90-entry shape.
datatype: void (*[90])(uint32)  (90 contiguous 32-bit LE function pointers; Ghidra datatype pointer[90])
element_semantics: Each element is a 32-bit code pointer to a chapter-event handler fd2_chapter_event_handler_NN__* with ABI void(uint32 char_idx) (single cdecl dword arg = active character/recipient index).
comment_original_issue: The src comment was accurate but listed only the 'Three readers' (the direct literal-base xref sites) and never mentioned the primary battle-AI dispatch path via the data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_idx latch -- i.e. the exact mechanism the symbol is named after. A reader of btltab.c could not tell why the symbol is named 'ai_post_action_consequence'.
notes: Ghidra datatype confirmed pointer[90]; live symbol name confirmed; data plate was null and is now created (PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline) reflecting the src conclusion. memory read of 360 bytes = 90 LE pointers all in 0x341DB..0x360FE. No writers anywhere (read-only at runtime), but declared non-const to match globals.h void(*[90])(uint32) extern and the function-pointer-table-placed-by-linker contract (Layer-2). Did not change any code/type/declaration; only augmented the symbol's comment block in btltab.c and created the Ghidra data plate.
